Commentary.Commentary: India are now right up against it. An entire session left today to play out. How their openers go about their business could tell how this chase might pan out. How will they approach this? Be more cautious? Or take a leaf out of Curran's book and attack? We'll find out soon enough when they come out after getting some fluids in. Don't go anywhere, we'll be right back!

The youngster Curran was oozing with confidence as he took the attack to the Indian bowlers. His quickfire 63 could just prove to be the turning point in this game. England were largely bundled up by a classy Ishant Sharma 5-fer and some more than handy assistance from Umesh Yadav and Ravichandran Ashwin. A lead of 150 would have been testing for the Indians with the swinging conditions, but now this has posed a different challenge altogether, and that can be attributed to some poor catching which cost them these runs.

TEA HAS BEEN TAKEN. You'd never have thought England would have got in this position after where they were before Sam Curran took charge of things. The last three wickets added 93 runs, and Sam Curran was responsible for scoring the bulk of those runs. Much like Virat Kohli yesterday, where 92 were scored by the last 2 wickets and he did most of the hitting.

OUT! ENGLAND ALL OUT FOR 180, SETTING A TARGET OF 194! Yadav angles across a back of a length ball outside off, Curran walks across a bit and then guides it behind towards Karthik. He catches the ball and then takes a needless tumble. End of a fantastic knock by Sam Curran, he though is disappointed in the manner he got out. The crowd is giving him a standing ovation. The young lad has kept England in the game.
Beaten! Good length ball on off, shaping away, Curran pushes inside the line and misses.
Field comes up.
FOUR! Up and over the infield. Back of a length ball around off, Curran stays back and powers his pull shot over mid on. He is batting like Virat Kohli did yesterday.
Another bumper. Curran ducks underneath it again.
Short and outside off, Curran plays it down to third man and denies a single.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under it at the last moment.
James Anderson is the last batsman for England.

OUT! Miracle, Dhawan has taken a catch! It's a 5-wicket haul for Ishant Sharma, 8th in Tests and 2nd against England. Top effort. He pitches this one up outside off and gets it to shape away. Broad is sucked into a drive through the line with a straight bat but edges it behind to Dhawan. He makes no mistake at first slip and then gets up to do his trademark thigh-slap. Hmmm...doesn't look too good when you have been dropping those. Anyway, England lead by 189 runs.
Play and a miss! Beautiful delivery. Angling in on a good length around off, Broad remains back to play at it but it nips away to beat the outside edge.
Fuller delivery angling in around off, Broad somehow keeps it out on the off side.
Shortish and angling in on middle and leg, Broad stays back and blocks it down safely.
Digs in a short ball outside off, Curran rises on his back foot and strokes it through point for a run.
Full and around off, eased off the back foot through backward point. An easy single.
Yadav goes closer to the off stump line, Broad pushes it through cover-point for a single. Another vital partnership for England, this one is worth 39. Lead is 187.
Another delivery in the channel outside off, Broad keeps himself on the back foot, pushes at it from there and gets beaten.
Yadav goes full and outside off, some visible away movement, Broad gets across and tries to push at it. Misses.
Back of a length ball on off, Broad goes back and gently pushes it through point for a couple of runs.
On a length around middle, Curran stays back and runs it down to deep backward point for a single.
Good length ball around leg, Curran glances it off his hips through square leg and scampers back for the second run.
Fullish and on middle and leg. Broad keeps it out off his pads to the leg side.
Back of a length delivery outside off, shaping away, Stuart pokes at it and misses.
Outside off, played through point for one.

A typical fast bowler's reply. Follows the batsman down the leg side with a lethal bouncer. Curran moves back, tries to sway away from the line of fire and eventually falls down as it goes to the keeper.

SIX! Smoking hot! What a way to get your first Test fifty! He gives the charge to the bowler, it's on the shorter side around middle and off and Curran clubs it over extra cover for a biggie. Raises his bat and the crowd is giving him a warm ovation. Lead is now 180!
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Ishant Sharma is back on.

What a terrific over! Beats Curran for the sixth time. Yadav has a wry smile on his face. Almost made him edge six times in this over. This delivery is on a length and wide outside off, Sam shuffles across the stumps but still fails to get bat on ball.
Five in a row. All that didn't help. Back of a length ball on off, moving away, Curran pushes inside the line and misses.

Make it four. Once again a length ball shapes away from the southpaw. Curran tries his best to put bat on ball but misses. Needs to catch a few breaths. Calm down. He does the sensible thing of moving across towards his partner. Has some words and then returns to his mark.
Another play and a miss. Three in a row. Umesh takes another length ball away from the batsman, Curran tries forcing it through the line and misses. Looks at the heavens in disappointment.
Beaten again. Full in length and around off, angling away, Curran pushes at it flat-footed and misses.
A length ball outside off, Curran flays at it and misses.
Sensible batting. Just knocks a full ball down to long on and retains strike with a single. Lead is just 27 short of 200.

FOUR! Taking the attack to Ashwin. This time he stays back in anticipation of a quicker delivery. Ashwin sends across a flatter one on off and Curran thwacks it down the ground for a boundary at long on.
SIX! High and handsome! Sam Curran is earning a lot of fans here. He is down the track in a flash to a full ball and hammers it over the bowler's head for a biggie.
Once again connects with his sweep shot and this time finds the gap through backward square leg. A single to bring Sam on strike.
Flatter and fuller on middle, jammed out by Broad.
Goes down on one knee and sweeps it straight to short fine leg.

FOUR! Curran has impressed a lot in this Test match. Useful runs with the bat in the first innings, a 4-fer with the ball and this knock can prove to be a potentially match-winning one. Yadav offers width outside off, Sam keeps his eyes on the ball and weight on the back leg. He then uses his long reach to guide it down to third man for a boundary.
Broad opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR BYES! Bonus runs for England! A bouncer by Yadav. Broad ducks and Karthik fails to collect it with a jump. India will be worried. These runs can hurt them.
Beaten! Back of a length ball angling away from the batsman. Broad jumps on his back foot as he pushes at it and misses.
A length ball around leg, Broad moves back to cover the line and defends it on the leg side.
Spears in a very full ball on middle, Broad keeps his eyes on the ball and keeps it out on the leg side.
Sliding down the leg side, Broad moves inside the crease and eases it behind to fine leg for another run.
This one is very full and on off, Broad jams it out back to the bowler.
Oh, well played. Broad goes down on one knee, fetches it from outside off and sweeps it through square leg for a couple of runs. Lead crosses 150!
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it with the spin towards cover-point.
Once again a watchful forward defense by Broad.
Loopy and full on off, Broad draws forward in defense.
Fullish and on middle, swinging down, Broad flicks it through square leg for a single.
Goes very full and around off, Broad defends it out safely.
Stuart Broad is in next. He is no mug with the bat either.

OUT! Right through the gate! A 135 kph delivery by Yadav. A rip-roaring one. He pitches it on a length around off, nipping in enough to breach Rashid's defense. It goes right through and uproots the off stump. A handy 48-run stand is broken. Nicely set up by Umesh, bowled a couple of outswingers and then brought one in to dismiss Rashid. England lead by 148!
Nice delivery. Angling into the batsman around off, Rashid plays the line and gets beaten by the away movement.
Play and a miss! It's still swinging. Yadav lets it out on a length outside off, a lazy waft by Adil and he misses.
Fullish and on the pads, Curran deflects it fine down the leg side for a run.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Nicely tossed up ball on middle and off, Curran defends it down.
Presses forward and pushes it with the spin to the off side.
Tossed up ball outside off, Curran swats it through the line and Pandya at covers makes a good stop.
Slower through the air, landing around off and skidding in, Sam is forward in defense.
Flighted and full around off, it's driven off the front foot to covers.
On a length and around off, Curran taps it down towards cover-point and takes a quick single.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Rashid eases it down to fine leg and crosses for a run.
Nipping away from a length around off, Rashid watches the line closely and then leaves it. Showing good temperament.
Better line this time. Umesh hurls it across on a length around off. Shaping away just a bit, Rashid is watertight in his defense.
This one is way wide outside off, further shaping away, an easy leave this time for Adil.
A length ball in the channel outside off, shaping away a bit, Rashid shoulders arms.
Back again! Virat Kohli sharing some words of wisdom with his teammates in a huddle. Out come Adil Rashid and Sam Curran. Umesh Yadav continues...

It has turned very gloomy out there. The floodlights are switched on but the umpires feel that the natural light is not enough to carry on with the game. The players are leaving the field while the umpires are taking the reading. A huge chunk of clouds are approaching the field. For the moment, BAD LIGHT HAS STOPPED PLAY. India won't mind this break. They were going wayward a bit after doing all the hard work. The current partnership is worth 44 and that has taken the lead to 144. Stay tuned for latest updates.
Full and flighted on off, it's flicked with the spin through mid-wicket for a run.
Leans forward to defend, plays for the inward spin there but it skids through to beat the outside edge.
Sharp spin back into the batsman, it's played down to leg gully.
Flatter and shorter around off, Rashid goes on the back foot and defends.
Strides forward to a full ball and defends it.
Flighted and around off, Rashid defends it off his back foot. This one drifted in a little bit and spun the other way. More like a carrom ball.
Speedy delivery, short and wide outside off, Curran slashes and misses.
Goes on the back foot and steers it through point for a single.

DROPPED! Dhawan at it again. Rashid is lured into the drive by Yadav. He tries to go through the line but gets a thick outside edge to Dhawan at first slip. Karthik for a moment moves to his right but then lets it through. Dhawan tries taking the catch near his chest but fails to hang on. Smiles after that. Maybe, for a fraction of a second, Shikhar got distracted by DK. Anyway, England won't mind.
Serves it full this time, outside off, Rashid drives it with an open face but finds the cover fielder.
Back of a length ball on off, Rashid is showing great technique. Eases his weight on the back foot, gets right behind the line of the delivery and blocks it to the off side.
Angles in a length ball on off, Rashid presses forward and gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Umesh Yadav to bowl for the first time in this innings.
Big spin away from the southpaw, Sam plants his front foot forward and leaves it alone.
FOUR! Fine shot! Curran spots the short delivery early, goes deep inside the crease and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Gets on the front foot and drives it back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted and full on off, Curran lets it go watchfully.
Flatter and on middle, it's defended off the back foot.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Rashid shoulders arms. Another good over for England, 10 from it. 19 in the last two and the lead is now 138 runs.

FOUR! Well played! A pitched up ball outside off, Rashid went for the drive through the line, opened the face of the bat a bit and placed it through backward point. It sped through and found the fence before the fielder in the deep got to it.
On a length and outside off, Rashid gets on the front foot and pushes it towards covers.
Sam can bat! A lovely back foot punch this time and he finds the gap at covers. The mid off fielder moves across to his right to make the stop. A single taken.

FOUR! Suddenly runs are coming thick and fast. As soon as Curran spots the room outside off, he throws his bat at it. The ball finds the outside edge but flies over the slip cordon for a boundary at third man.
Lands it on a length and around off, Rashid gets forward and plays at it late. Drives it nicely through point and collects a run. Doing it easily, Adil. The partnership moves to 29 now.
Shortish and on middle, Curran fails to work it around and is hit on the thigh pad.

FOUR! Once again streaky! Shami darts in a length ball on off and gets it to straighten after landing, Curran gets completely squared up and edges it behind. Right through the slip cordon for another useful boundary. Lead is now 128!
Short ball outside off, played down to point.

FOUR! Welcome boundary for England. Was that a chance? Yeah. But Dhawan fails to get any hand on it. Short in length and outside off, Curran stands back to slap it through the line but it takes the bottom edge and flies behind. Dhawan goes down low at first slip but it sneaks past his hands, maybe just brushed his fingers, before racing away.
Short in length and outside off, Adil goes on his back foot and runs it down through backward point for one.
Full and outside off, pushed to the off side by Rashid.
Beauty! Ishant angles it away from the left-hander from over the wicket. It pitches on off and nips away. Curran tries playing the line but is beaten by the away movement.
Wayward delivery. Short and angling down the leg side, Rashid goes for the pull but fails to middle it. The ball goes off his gloves to fine leg and the batsmen change ends.
Ishant digs in a short ball around off and Rashid pulls it through backward square leg. A couple more added to the total. Lead is now 118!
Plays a length ball from the crease but finds the fielder at point.
Angles in a full ball just around off, Rashid is on the front foot as he defends it solidly.
Drifting down the leg side, sharp pace. Rashid tries flicking but misses. It goes off his pads to Karthik who flies to his left and stops the ball albeit not cleanly. No run taken though.
Play and a miss! Lands it on a length and outside off, holding its line, Curran pokes inside the line and misses.
Bouncer around off, Curran sits underneath it.
Shami overpitches this time. Around off and Sam pushes it gently to point.
Back of a length delivery around off, Curran eases himself on the back foot and punches it square of the wicket on the off side. Another couple added to the lead. Every run matters.
Sharp delivery. Shami brings a length ball into the left-hander with the angle from 'round the wicket. Curran defends it to mid-wicket.
Shortish and on middle, Rashid goes on his toes and tickles it behind square leg for a run.
FOUR! Well played! Ishant overpitches and Curran latches onto it like a hawk on its prey. Plays a full-blooded cover drive and it races away to the fence. The 100 comes up for England.
Angling into the batsman, on a length, Curran once again presents a straight bat in defense.
Quite assured in defense, Sam. Ishant serves it full and around off this time, Curran with gentle hands defends it watchfully.
Identical to the last delivery. Once again it's going down the leg side and Curran fails to get any wood behind it.
Loses control. Runs in from 'round the wicket and slips a shortish length ball down the leg side. Curran tries flicking but misses.
Slants in a good length ball on middle and leg, Curran covers the line and dead bats it back to the bowler.
Goes full this time. Arrows it on around off, nipping away slightly, Rashid presses forward and blocks it safely to the off side.

Bends his back and digs in a short ball outside off. A little bit of away movement even on this one. Rashid tries to pull but fails to middle it properly. It takes the bottom half and rolls on the leg side.
Nice shot! Around off on a length, Rashid is on the front foot as he drives it on the up. Finds the gap through cover-point and picks up a couple of runs.
A length ball on off, Adil covers the line and movement before offering a straight blade in defense.
Width on offer outside off, Curran remains back footed and steers it through point for one.
Angles in a good length ball on off, Curran sticks back inside the crease in defense.
Bowling change. Mohammed Shami replaces Ashwin in the attack.
Nearly draws a false shot! Once again Ishant bowls it wide outside off, Rashid goes chasing after it but fails to connect.
Loses control this time, Sharma. Sprays it wide outside off and Adil allows it through.

A little short in length and around middle and leg, Curran works it in the gap at mid-wicket and rotates the strike. England will be aiming to get somewhere near 150 at least. The way it's still moving around, it isn't going to be easy for India either.
Lands it on a length outside off, shaping in a bit, Rashid pushes it with gentle hands to covers and picks up a quick single.
Bouncer and outside off, it's left alone by Rashid.
Good length ball on off, angling in, Adil gets behind the line and blocks it off his back foot.
Skidding back in from around off, Curran defends it off his back foot.
Flatter and on off, defended off the back foot.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Once again the length is on the fuller side around off and Curran drives it straight back past the bowler for a boundary down the ground. Useful runs.
Tossed up ball on middle, defended on the leg side.
Full and flighted on off, defended off the front foot.
Adil Rashid is in next.

OUT! Another blow to England, Ishant has his third wicket in the over and has completely demolished the home team. There goes England's last recognized batsman. What a spell! He worked hard initially and is finally getting the rewards. This one is more on the lines of a poor shot than a great delivery. Short and wide outside off, Buttler has the option to leave it but his natural instinct is always to go after the ball. He does that. Stays back inside the crease to flash his bat through the line. Gets a faint outside edge behind and Dinesh Karthik hangs on to the catch. The umpire checks for the front foot no ball and Ishant is just fine with his landing. The lead is of 100.
A bit short and around leg, Curran turns it off his pads through square leg for a single. Lead - 100 runs.

We are back. The men concerned are back on the field. The Indian players get into a huddle before dispersing on the field. Sam Curran is the new batsman who has joined Buttler in the middle. Ishant Sharma to complete his over.
... DAY 3, SECOND SESSION ...

The lead is just of 99 at the moment. The visitors have entered the tail and if more of the same is expected, which you can bet it is, then England are in for a rough ride. Jos Buttler is a fine batsman, but in this format and in such conditions, even he has a uphill task ahead of him. Join us for all the action from the afternoon session at 1340 local (1240 GMT). You don't want to miss it...

Like in the final minutes of Day 2, Ravichandran Ashwin started the day's proceedings with a bang. Got Keaton Jennings out early and followed it up with the big wicket of Joe Root. Dawid Malan and Jonny Bairstow steadied the ship, but it didn't last long as Ishant Sharma was on a different level altogether today. First got Malan, then kept the pressure on and got Bairstow, before eventually sending Ben Stokes back right at the stroke of the break. This is what good, penetrating bowling can do for you, he's put his side in a commanding position.

Heroes are there for a reason. They are born out of adversity and rise up from the ashes, inspiring others in the process as well. That's what happened in Birmingham. Yesterday, Virat Kohli put on a fighting display for the world to see, gave him confidence to lift their levels up and has got the response he was looking for. His Indian side has come out firing since the morning began and took this game right by the scruff of its neck.

OUT! Ishant has another one. This is brilliant, brilliant bowling from the tall pacer. Terrific, terrific stuff. Comes from around the wicket and angles in a length ball on off. Much like Malan's wicket, this one also straightens up and gets Big Ben. He hangs his bat out to defend, edges it and it's taken by skipper Virat Kohli at at third slip, by diving low to his left. Ishant is screaming in joy, Kohli is all pumped up. India all over England like a rash. Also, it's time for LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Off the mark without wasting any time. Length ball aiming the top of off stump, tucked behind square leg for a single.
Jos Buttler to be the new man in for England.

OUT! This time Ishant gets his man. That is an excellent catch from Shikhar Dhawan at first slip. Length delivery around off, shaping in and Bairstow hangs his bat inside the line. Gets a healthy edge which goes behind. Dhawan gets low to his right and collects it safely. Superb stuff. India in the driver's seat here. Mainly because they've got Jonny Bairstow, who's an excellent player of spin. England's lead is just two short of 100.
Extra bounce for Ishant as he comes around the wicket. It's down leg though. Karthik moves to his right but can't collect it. A bye has been stolen.
No spin on this one, outside off, left alone.
Straighter one on off from over the wicket, Bairstow turns it in front of short leg.
Too straight once more, Ben Stokes once again plays it off the back foot. Whips it to deep square leg. One run collected.
On the leg stump line again, tucked past Shami at backward square leg for two more.
Landed shorter around off, turning away, Stokes moves across to get behind the line and defends.
Drifting in on leg, on a shorter length, Stokes goes back and nudges it past backward square leg. Shami chases it and keeps the batsmen down to two.

Very good delivery to end the over. Ishant draws the edge by bowling a full swinging delivery which comes into the batsman. Jonny Bairstow tries to drive it through the covers but gets an edge which falls short of the first slip fielder.
Comfortable leave, this. On a fourth stump line, it's left alone for the keeper to collect.

FOUR! Almost dragged it on! A boundary results but he's lucky he's survived that. Back of a length close to off, Bairstow looks to cut but gets it off the inside edge past the off stump. Karthik dives to his left but can't stop it.
Coming in again, defended out once more. Maybe the next one goes the other way?
Full in length, coming in and attacking the off pole, Bairstow brings down a straight blade in defense and keeps it out.
Fired full and well outside off, Bairstow has nothing to do with it.
Drives the full ball outside off to the sub Jadeja at covers.
The slider from Ashwin, but Stokes is up for it. He keeps bat and pad close together and blocks it out.
Turning away from a full length, around off, Stokes lets it be.
Comes from around the wicket to Stokes, bowls it full, it's kept out.
Goes on the back foot, plays with the turn and works it past short leg for one.
Top edge but safe. Bairstow kneels down to sweep it away but gets a top edge over the keeper's head. Two runs taken.
Searching for that magic yorker as Ishant bowls an inswinging delivery on leg, Bairstow flicks it down to fine leg for a single.
Off the mark with a single. Stokes uses the angle and works it away on the leg side to change ends.
Should India get an extra catcher in? Around 20 minutes to the break, another breakthrough would be golden for them.
Comes half-forward to this one and keeps it out.
Length delivery just outside off, straightening up, Stokes covers the line and makes a leave.
Ben Stokes walks out to the middle next. England in trouble here, can't afford another wicket before the break. This pair needs to hang on.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Ishant Sharma has been rewarded for the good bowling he's been doing so far. Totally on fire since the time he's come on, got the results for it with this wicket. Comes from around the wicket and angles in a length ball on off. It straightens up enough after landing, a little late and that does Dawid Malan in. He is squared up as he looks to flick and gets it off the leading edge towards Rahane at gully, who makes no mistake in taking that. England lead by 83 runs.

A little dangerous again but Bairstow executes it well this time. Closes the face of the blade to this full ball swinging in and flicks it through the vacant spaces in the mid-wicket region. A single results.
Goes against the spin and flicks it through the mid-wicket area for a double.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Outside off, left alone.
Watches the ball cautiously as he defends it down on the off side.
An erratic shout from Ashwin for a leg before but nothing from the umpire. Probably because Malan is too far down the track. Uses his feet to flick the ball coming in, misses and is hit on the pads.
A bit of extra bounce as Ashwin bowls the slider on middle. It keeps going straight and goes off the top half of Malan's bat through the vacant silly point position.
Driven a bit square and Bairstow will pick up a couple. Places it through cover-point and comes back for the second. Steady partnership building here, worth 28 as of now.
Way outside off, no trouble for the right-hander to not bother himself with it.
Solidly done this time. Full and curling in on off, driven back in the bowler's direction.
Offers some width outside off, on a length, Bairstow tries to flay this away but fails to make connection.

Almost got him. That was close. Bairstow needs to be careful. Not the brightest of ideas to play across the line when the ball is swinging in like it is right now. Full on middle, Jonny attempts to flick it through mid-wicket but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Ishant tempts Bairstow with a loosener outside off. Full and wide, but the batsman doesn't fiddle with it.
Malan has nothing to do with this as the ball lands on off and turns away into the keeper's gloves.
Spinning away from middle stump, on a driving length, guarded out safely.
Leans ahead to this fullish length delivery and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Ashwin is doing a good job of making him play more. Keeps it close to off and tosses it up there, blocked off the front foot.
Lateral turn away from around off, Dawid shoulders arms to it.
A lot of air on this one as it's pitched on off, drifts in and Malan blocks.
FOUR! No third man and that's a boundary. Good way to end the over. Bairstow has some room to work with, he wastes no time in cutting this across the third man fence. Nicely done.
Throws this well outside off, no shot offered from the batsman on this occasion.
Pitches it on a fuller length on off, makes it come back in again, it's driven without great timing towards mid off.

FOUR! That's right in the gap. Superb shot from Jonny Bairstow. Length ball outside off, he cuts this through point and finds the boundary line. Positive from Bairstow so far, important to not get too defensive.
A little too much swing on this occasion. It goes down the leg side, Bairstow misses the flick and it's a good take by Karthik who dives a long way to his left and catches it.
A lot of swing for Ishant Sharma. He looks like he might do some damage here. Comes charging in and bowls it full outside off, it tails in heavily as Bairstow blocks it out on the off side.
Harmless delivery outside off, left alone to end the over.
Goes with the spin and drives it to the cover region.
Serves it well outside off, Dawid lets it be as it spins away.
Drifting in at first before turning away on off, the southpaw is well behind the line to block.
Nicely tossed up, a lot of flight on that, outside off. Malan drives it hard right at the man at short cover.
Drifting in on a fuller length on off, Malan comes forward and blocks it out off the inner half.
Fuller in length, tailing back in and attacking the stumps, Bairstow pushes it back down the track. End of the over.
Over the wicket to the right-hander, full and swinging back in on middle, Jonny Bairstow drives it to mid on.
Back of a length delivery which doesn't rise as much as expected, Malan stands tall and drags the pull through mid-wicket for a single.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Continues from around the wicket and bowls it on a length outside off, it moves away and shoots off the deck. Karthik moves to his left and collects it well.
Bowls it on a length and outside off, Malan keeps his bat close to his body and leaves it.

Interesting. Bairstow premeditates the sweep shot but finds the line not good enough to play that shot. He then thinks about driving but is late to it. As a last resort, he blocks it at the very last moment. It goes off the inner half of the bat and just misses the stumps.
Turning down the leg side, Jonny tries to flick but misses.
FOUR! Bang! Ashwin is on the shorter side outside off, turning back in, Bairstow goes deep inside the crease and whacks it square of the wicket on the off side for a boundary.

Ouch, that would have hurt Vijay. A full-blooded sweep shot from Jonny and it hits Vijay flush on his body at short leg. The ball rebounds and Karthik tries to take it with a dive across to his left. Fails to reach though. Vijay is fine.
Gets on the front foot and defends it watchfully.
Tossed up ball on off, defended on the leg side.

Drinks break. Eventful first hour for India. They have bagged a couple of wickets which includes the prized scalp of Joe Root. Their bowlers have been right on the money, especially Ravichandran Ashwin, who has utilized the conditions to full advantage. England have their backs to the wall as their lead is only 65 at this stage.

NOT OUT! That has hit the ground. Ishant nearly had his first wicket. Slants in a full length ball on off and gets it to curl away. Malan who has been completely clueless once again plays inside the line and it takes the outside edge. It flies behind and Dhawan at first slip goes down low to grab the ball. He though is not too sure and hence the umpires get together to have a chat before going upstairs. Umpire Dar gives it not out as the soft signal. The replays roll in and they find that the ball has grazed the grass.
Has that carried? Shikhar Dhawan takes a low catch at first slip and is not sure whether it carried. The umpires get together and then take it upstairs. Aleem Dar gives the soft signal as not out.
And he does. Lands it full and just outside off, Malan once again remains on the back foot, gets squared up a bit and is beaten by the away movement.
Peach of a delivery. Ishant angles in a length ball around off, nipping away sharply after landing. Malan with zero footwork pushes at it and misses. Needs to get a bit fuller.
Delivers it on a length and outside off, shaping away a bit, Malan keeps his bat close to the body and allows it through.
A length ball angling down the leg side, Malan tries to flick but misses. It goes behind off his pads and Karthik dives across to his right to make a half stop.
A deep square leg in place as Ishant Sharma changes his angle for Dawid Malan.

Excellent delivery. Ishant gets it to move back into the batsman big time. Jonny tries working it around but gets an inside edge on his thigh pad. It drops near the surface and they cross for a quick run.
Flashes and misses! Fuller in length and wide outside off, Bairstow tries to drive but misses. Called a no ball for overstepping.
Ishant Sharma to bowl now, replacing Mohammed Shami.
Dawid has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Another top over from a top bowler.
Tossed up and outside off, spinning away, Malan leaves.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball around off and blocks.

Shout for an lbw! A nicely tossed up ball this time. An off spinner landing full around leg. Malan leans forward to defend but misses to get hit high on the back leg. They appeal but nothing from the umpire. The replays show that it marginally landed outside leg.
Fires this one in, at 92 kph, it lands on the shorter side around off and skids down sharply, Malan goes deep inside the crease and blocks.
Flighted off spinner, landing full around off and spins away slightly. Malan gets forward and jams it down at the last moment off the shoulder of his bat.
FOUR! Shot! Boundary to end the over and the 50 comes up for England. Overpitched around off from over the wicket, Jonny Bairstow drives it nicely through the covers and finds the fence.
Taps this square on the off side to point and takes a single.

Whoa! That was mighty close. Even Malan knows that, he has a wry smile on his face. Shami angles it in from around off, Malan just about covers the line as he shoulders arms to it. The ball whizzes past the top of the off stick.
Just ahead of a length around off, kept out off the front foot.
FOUR! Good control from Malan. Shami bangs it short from around the wicket and brings it in, Malan uses the angle to swivel inside and pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary.
Angling back in on a good length, goes off Bairstow's pads who tries working it across the line. A leg bye is taken as the ball rolls to square leg.
Brave, brave leave. Nicely tossed up outside off, it keeps on skidding towards off as Malan makes the leave. That wasn't very far from the off pole. What an over by Ash!
Quicker and full on off, defended off the front foot.
Turning back in sharply again, Bairstow fails to flick and it goes off his pads past the leg gully fielder. A leg bye taken.
Jonny has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Nearly another sharp catch by KL. Bairstow flicks it from the full face of the bat towards leg gully where Rahul dives but it falls short.
Jonny Bairstow arrives with England leading by 52 runs.

OUT! Massive breakthrough for the touring team. Ashwin has hunted down the big fish this time. Talk about the catch. Tremendous reflexes shown by KL Rahul. He has taken yet another sharp catch. He is up and running in celebration. Root also starts to walk after looking down for a moment in disbelief. The umpire has a little word with the English skipper, maybe on what exactly happened. Seems Root is sure that the catch is taken cleanly as he keeps on walking. Big blow to England. Coming to the delivery, it's a bit on the shorter side and turns back in sharply with extra bounce. Root tries flicking and does so straight towards Rahul at leg gully. He reacts quickly and somehow hangs onto it. India are roaring now.
What happened there? India are celebrating. Root is seen walking. Has a word with the umpire then but after that he continues to walk.
Delivers it short and outside off, from over the wicket, Root leans back and guides it down to third man for a run.

Wild one. A wayward delivery. Shami loses his radar and bowls it way wide down the leg side. Malan swings his bat at it but misses. Karthik does well to dive across to his right to stop the ball. Not a clean stop though and hence the batsmen steal a bye.
Good length delivery landing outside off and once again nipping back in off the seam. Malan covers his stumps and shoulders arms.
Full and around off, Malan has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Nearly edges it. A bit of a sound but not bat. Excellent length from Shami. Keeps it just outside off, angling back in, Malan commits himself forward and tries to push inside the line. Misses. The sound was of the bat hitting the pad.
Extra bounce this time as Shami angles in a good length ball from 'round the wicket. Malan tries to work it on the leg side but misses. Takes a hit on his thigh pad.
A flighted off spinner landing full on off, Joe gets forward to play the flick shot but finds Kohli at mid-wicket.
Tossed up ball on off, defended nicely off the front foot.

FOUR! Ashwin stays over the wicket for the right-hander also. Bowls it short and around off, turning back in, Root immediately pushes his weight on the back foot and slaps it through covers for a boundary. Lead is now 50!
Switches to over the wicket for the left-hander. Interesting ploy from Ashwin. Serves it full on leg though and Malan helps it wide of mid on for a run.
Loopy and full around leg, Root leans forward and flicks it in front of square leg for a single.
From 'round the wicket, Ashwin bowls it shorter and on middle, Root goes back and works it on the leg side.
The line is too straight this time, fuller in length and Joe flicks it through backward square leg for a single.
Goes full this time and around off, Root pushes it out towards the cover fielder.

Shami goes wide of the crease this time. Angles in a length ball outside off and it shapes away after landing. Root has an easy leave. This delivery would have troubled the English skipper had Shami bowled it close to the off stump line.
Good length ball around off, angling in, Root covers the line and blocks it. The ball drops near the surface and rolls behind. Joe immediately turns to see it go wide of the stumps.
Pitches it up and outside off, a delightful cover drive from Root but he finds Pandya.
Angles in a length ball on off, Root defends it to the off side.
Ashwin comes from over the wicket now. Delivers an off spinner around the middle stump line. Malan tries defending it by getting forward but is beaten as it spins past the outside edge.
Loopy and full around off, Root is on the front foot as he flicks it with the spin. Goes past the short leg fielder and they rush across for a run.
A drive off the front foot this time, with the spin he goes and finds the gap at covers. A single taken.
Here it comes. Skidding back in from around off, Dawid picks it correctly and blocks it back.
Another one turning away from the left-hander, Malan allows it through. Watch out for the slider.
Flighted and outside off, spinning away, Malan leaves it.
On a length and close to the off stump line, Root sticks back inside the crease and blocks it out on the off side.
Fullish and outside off, it's driven down the ground but straight towards mid off.
Good length ball around off, Joe remains on the back foot and defends it back.
Short and angling into the batsman from around off, Malan pulls it behind square leg for a single.
Pitches it up and around off, Dawid defends it off his front foot.
Play and a miss! Loose, very loose by Malan. Goes chasing at a short ball wide outside off and misses. Nearly got an outside edge.
Tossed up and on off, driven down to mid on to end the over.
This time the line is straighter as it skids towards Malan's pads. He works it behind square leg for a single.
Loopy around off and spinning away, Malan lets it be.
Takes a stride forward and drives it with the spin to covers.
Once again Malan is on the front foot in defense.
Full and flighted on off, defended off the front foot.
Fullish and outside off, driven towards mid off to end the over.
An outswinger outside off, curling away, Root allows it through to the keeper.
Full and around off, angling in, Malan gets forward and across to flick it towards mid-wicket for a single.

EDGY FOUR! Malan though did well to play it with soft hands. A length ball angling back into the batsman from around off, Dawid plays it late and close to his body. It takes the outside edge and runs past the slip cordon for a boundary.
Another delivery in the channel of uncertainty. Malan lets it be.
Shami dishes out a full length ball outside off. Malan lets it be. Some inward movement again.
Turning back in from around off, Joe sticks back inside the crease to keep it out. End of a successful over for India.
A bit risky. Reaches out for a delivery wide outside off and drives it through the line. A bit uppish but through the gap to sweeper cover. Three runs to get off the mark, Dawid will feel relieved.
Here comes Dawid Malan. Two dropped catches yesterday, both of Virat Kohli. Pressure on him. Can he deliver?

OUT! This was coming! Superbly bowled by Ashwin. He gives this one a good toss in the air and lands it full around off. Jennings has no option but to play at it as it's drifting in. He leans forward to defend with a straight bat but to his bad luck, it spins away and takes the outside edge. KL Rahul at second slip stretches his hands to his right and grabs a sharp catch. Early success for India. England lead by 31 runs and have both their openers back in the hut. On this wicket, an interesting point made by the on-air commentator. Jennings is seen taking a long stride forward and going at the ball, rather than allowing it to come at him. Joe Root, on the other hand, would have mostly played it late from the back. Another valid point made is that Keaton's effort is mainly to avoid DRS as he takes his bat ahead of the front pad to avoid the lbw.
Loopy and full around off, from 'round the wicket, Jennings defends it off his front foot.
That's nicely played. Root uses his feet to make the length fuller and drives it down the ground. The deepish mid on fielder moves across to his left to stop the ball and they take a single.
Flighted and full outside off, Root prefers to defend it off his back foot. Should have been forward there.
Excellent delivery and a good leave. Shami serves it on a good length outside off, shaping back in, Keaton guards his stumps and shoulders arms.

That was oh so close to the outside edge. Shami bowls it on a length and outside off, straightening a bit, Jennings has a needless push inside the line and misses. For a moment, we thought there was some nick but nothing from the Indian fielders. Would love to see the Snicko for this delivery.
Switches again to 'round the wicket for Jennings. Serves a length ball around middle and off, it's been worked straight towards the fielder standing in front of square leg.
Shami goes for the yorker but gets it all wrong. A low full toss on the pads has been deflected down to fine leg by Root for a single.

A pitched up ball this time, Jennings drives it square of the wicket on the off side. Pandya rushes behind it and slides to stop the ball. Root initially eyes the second run but then sends his partner back.

Shami operating from over the wicket for Jennings now. He runs in and delivers a length ball wide outside off. Some visible movement there as it lands and straightens. Keaton though has left it alone.
Shortish and around off, turning back in, Root goes deep inside the crease and keeps it out on the off side.
This one doesn't land. Root flicks a low full toss across the line but finds the mid-wicket fielder yet again.
Bowls this one on the middle stump line, Root works it with the spin but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Full this time, another off spinner, Joe is on the front foot in defense. Mixing his length, Ashwin.
An off spinner this time to Root. Turning in from around off, Root defends it off his back foot.
Lovely delivery and it has been played nicely too. Ashwin slows this one in the air and drops it on a fuller length around leg, Jennings sweeps it towards fine leg for a single.
Once again the angle from 'round the wicket is quite straight from Shami. Easy pickings for Keaton as he nudges it to fine leg for a run.
Shami switches to 'round the wicket for the left-hander. Fails to control his line first up and slips a length ball down the leg side. Keaton allows it through.

This one is on a length just around off, Root could have been forward there but decides to play at it from behind the crease. He just taps it down towards cover-point and scampers across to the other end. The fielder gets to the ball there, has a shy as well towards the striker's end but while doing so he is not in balance and hence it's wayward. Anyway, that would not have mattered much. Jennings was safely in.
A hint of movement on this occasion but the line is around middle, Root works it off his pads past the mid-wicket fielder. A couple of runs taken.
Another delivery around off, Root is forward as he blocks it watchfully.

Lands it on a length around off, Joe is on the front foot as he blocks it to the off side. There was little something in the pitch whole day yesterday, let's see what it has got to offer. The grass is looking quite brown and the deck on the drier side.
Mohammed Shami to continue from the other end. Three slips in place.
Turn and bounce for Ashwin. Root stays back inside the crease and does well by playing it off his pads to fine leg. Gets off the mark with a single.
Starts with a flighted full ball around off, Root leans forward and presents a straight bat in defense.

All set to get underway. Bright and sunny conditions. Looks a good day for batting. The players are taking the field. Skipper Joe Root is the new batsman and will be on strike. Keaton Jennings is at the other end. Ravichandran Ashwin to finish his over, two balls left. A slip, leg gully and short leg in place. Here we go...

Pitch Report - Sanjay Manjrekar out there in the middle again, looks at the pitch and says it's more or less the same from Day 2. Explaining the difference between English and Indian pitches, states that on the former there is dry grass so the ball doesn't skid because of the carpety nature, unlike India. Adds when the cover of grass is disturbed, where the soil is exposed, the spinners can exploit those areas. Ends by saying that Virat Kohli's heroics have given India a fighting chance and they can make a move on today.

What Kohli did right? Here's Sanjay Manjrekar analyzing it. He first tells us that Kohli is seen taking a big stride forward from the off stump line and it has helped him a little bit. Adds that yesterday every time when Kohli was looking to put bat to ball against James Anderson, most of the times it was getting edged behind. Hence, Manjrekar feels that Virat has not completely conquered Anderson. Advice from Sanjay Manjrekar who himself was considered to be a very technically sound batsman of his generation - He points out that the Indian skipper has this tendency to open the face of the bat quite often. Manjrekar suggests that Virat should present a straighter willow while trying to play close to his body. Mentions that playing with an angled bat is always going to be risky against a bowler like James Anderson. Reiterates that the bat needs to come a lot straighter and unless Kohli improves, the edges will keep coming. Ends by talking about the mental toughness which he considers is the key and as long as Virat Kohli has that, runs will come.

Virat Kohli has single-handedly kept India on top in this Test match after his batsmen were put to a stern test by the likes of Sam Curran, James Anderson and Ben Stokes. England will be ruing the dropped catches and Dawid Malan, in particular, would be feeling the heat. He will feel even more pressure today when he will come out to bat. The hosts are effectively 22/1 in this Test match which has turned into a one-innings shootout. Batting last in any Test ain't easy, that's why India can least afford to relax. Their aim will be to restrict the home team to a low total and for that to happen, their bowlers once again will have to deliver. Sets up to be another day of cracking Test cricket. Stay with us for all the updates.

If you opened the newspapers this morning or logged in to your social media accounts or just brought cricket as a topic of conversation with friends - I'm sure there would have been only one name doing the rounds - Virat Kohli. He's called King Kohli by his fans and most definitely the King conquered his final frontier on Day 2. A knock of character. A knock of determination. A knock of grit. A knock of craft. A knock of class. Scoring 149 runs when your other teammates were sent back to the pavilion with their tails between their legs, speaks volumes about the skipper's heroics. On that note, let me welcome you all for the coverage of the third day of the Edgbaston Test.
...DAY 3, FIRST SESSION...

The wicket of Alastair Cook just before stumps is the icing on the cake as India end the day's play once again in a dominating position, just like yesterday. The pendulum swung towards England in the first two sessions but Kohli's heroics have single-handedly forced the momentum back in their court. This Test match hangs in balance with England effectively 22 for 1 and Day 3 promises to be enthralling. Do join us at 1100 local (1000 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!

Despite losing partners at the other end, the Indian skipper kept going strongly. He raised a handy partnership with Hardik Pandya and then accumulated 92 runs with the last two batsmen. He made England pay big time for a couple of drops as he notched up his maiden Test century in this part of the world. Courtesy his masterly knock, England only managed a 13-run lead which at one stage hinted to be much more.

India were in all sorts of trouble heading into the Lunch break but had two of the most accomplished batsmen in Ajinkya Rahane and Virat Kohli unbeaten at the crease. However, the pair didn't last long. Ben Stokes bowled an excellent spell of seam bowling where he made the ball talk. He gave a glimpse of Andrew Flintoff in his effort and claimed the wickets of Rahane and Dinesh Karthik. James Anderson was an unlucky bowler, to be honest. There was a costly drop off his bowling by Dawid Malan and Virat Kohli was the beneficiary of that.

What a day of Test cricket! A satisfying one for the purists. It was an action-packed one, filled with all the drama and entertainment. At the start, India wasted no time in picking England's last wicket. Then they came out to bat and their openers saw off the new ball quite decently. The pair of Murali Vijay and Shikhar Dhawan laid a decent platform but what followed next was nothing less than spectacular. A 20-year old swing bowler, Sam Curran, sent the English crowd into a frenzy by running through India's top order in no time. His spell reminded many of the great Wasim Akram with whom Sam coincidentally shares his birthday and he surely made the legend proud.

OUT! Sound of timber! Action replay, Cook has been served the exact same menu to which he got out in the first innings! Ashwin has got Cook's number, has dismissed him 9 times in Tests now. Plenty of drift on this one as it lands on middle and spins away. Cook is forward in defense, tries to play the trajectory but is beaten by the turn. It goes past the outside half of his bat and hits the top of off stump. The Indian players are jumping up and down in celebration. They certainly know that it's a big wicket for them before the end of day's play. A duck for Alastair Cook and that will be Stumps on Day 2.
Full floated on off, Cook lunges and pushes it to covers.
Skidding down the leg side, Jennings eases it past short leg and gets to the other end.
Tossed up ball around off, spinning away, Jennings plays from the crease to point. This could be the last over of the day.
Shami goes full and gets some movement going. It curls back into the southpaw who just brings his bat down to keep it out towards mid on.
Identical to the last delivery, this time Cook is quite assure on his back foot as he leaves it alone.
Excellent line on this occasion. Bowls it on a shortish length around off and gets it to angle in, Cook stays back to play inside the line and misses.

Shami goes short this time but loses his line badly. Slips it down the leg side and Cook has nothing to do with it. Adil Rashid is seen wearing his pads. An indication that he will be the nightwatchman if a wicket goes down.

Shami runs in from 'round the wicket and serves a gentle length ball outside off. A hint of inward shape there but not enough to bother the English ex-skipper. He leaves it alone after covering the line.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Ashwin darts this one in at 96 kph, around off, Keaton Jennings stays back footed in defense.
Beaten! Ashwin gives this one some air and it drifts into the batsman. Jennings lunges to defend but it spins past his bat. Even the new ball is breaking free.
Tossed up ball on off, Keaton defends it off his front foot.
Loopy and outside off, it's been left alone by Jennings.
FOUR! This is a poor delivery. Ashwin bowls this one full and wide outside off, Keaton reaches out for it and strokes it through covers for a boundary.
A slider first up, around off and skidding in, Jennings gets forward to drive but it takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads. Needs to be careful.
Ravichandran Ashwin to bowl from the other end.
Stays right behind the line and blocks it out.
Alastair Cook chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Oooof! Almost! Shami lands it in the zone of apprehension, Cook has a tame poke at it from inside the line and almost nicks it behind. That was super close.
FOUR BYES! Shami keeps coming from around the wicket and angles it down the leg side once more. This one is too much, even for Karthik to collect, and the batsmen get byes as a result.
Another one down the leg side, Cook once more attempts to play at it but fails to do so.
Angling down the leg side, Cook looks to flick but misses.
